significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, despite cross-form storage invariance, query-form-specific router-head activity causally and predictively determines whether the same fact is recalled; this is form (iii) through the stated predictive coupling that router activation "predicts per-example success," reinforced by a form-(ii) causal claim. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—correct recall changing across "declarative cloze vs. interrogative vs. indirect/paraphrased vs. multiple-choice" forms—and a mechanism that distinguishes access failure from storage failure, thereby fixing expectations for selective head ablations, rephrasings, and repair; this distinction is consequential for the enrichment/extraction account in Geva et al.'s 2023 factual-recall work and for interpreting paraphrase failures in knowledge editing. The claim is determinate, and a negative result would meaningfully rule out the sparse-router explanation, although it would not by itself choose among distributed routing, semantic-processing, and genuine storage alternatives. In the topic-substitution check, the topic alone supports only the obvious hypothesis that retrieval depends on the query; the sparse causal routers, cross-form storage/retrieval decomposition, and predictive coupling are claim-specific and justify a score above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "RetrievalDivergence score," activation of query-form "router" heads as a predictor, and the "form-transfer intervention" that injects an easy-form retrieval direction into a failing form. The activation predictor is ex ante because it is available while the query is being processed, before recall success is observed, and can trigger reformatting or intervention; RetrievalDivergence is primarily post hoc, while form transfer is an inference-time repair handle. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction—that higher router activity forecasts cross-form success and selective router disruption causes failure—can transfer as a relation, although the particular heads and directions are not claimed to remain fixed across architectures. The hypothesis is framed across LLMs and several query forms, with likely uptake by interpretability researchers and model auditors rather than outside-AI users; after topic substitution these concrete predictor and intervention handles disappear, so the reach score is not being awarded for the broad knowledge-retrieval topic itself.
